hypothesis: Setup: /dev/rtc0 is a PNP0b00 CMOS RTC (rtc_cmos driver) at I/O 0x70-0x71, 114-byte NVRAM
test: Inspect sysfs tree, driver, resources, permissions
notes: PNP0b00 = CMOS RTC. NVRAM=114 bytes. /dev/rtc0 root-only. No rtcwake/hwclock binaries available.

hypothesis: /dev/rtc (symlink) and /dev/rtc0 are the same physical device
test: Compare device numbers of both paths
notes: Both point to major 249 minor 0. /dev/rtc -> rtc0.

hypothesis: RTC ioctls (RTC_RD_TIME, RTC_ALM_READ, RTC_WKALM_RD, RTC_IRQP_READ) work on this device
test: Probe each ioctl with root privileges
notes: RTC_EPOCH, RTC_VL, RTC_AIE_ON/OFF, RTC_UIE_ON/OFF, RTC_PIE_ON/OFF not supported. RTC_SET_TIME unsupported via ioctl.

hypothesis: RTC alarm is pre-set to 19:22:39 today (19:22:39)
notes: Alarm registers at 0x01/0x03/0x05 contain 0x39 0x22 0x19 (BCD for 19:22:39). Wakealarm timestamp 1795187430 = Fri Nov 20 15:22:30 UTC.

hypothesis: RTC periodic IRQ frequency is fixed at 1024 Hz (standard CMOS)
notes: 1024 Hz matches max_user_freq sysfs value. Driver doesn't allow setting (RTC_IRQP_SET untested).

hypothesis: RTC_SET_TIME cannot set the hardware clock time via ioctl
test: Probed RTC_SET_TIME with modified time, checked errno
notes: Errno 25 (Inappropriate ioctl) - driver does not support setting time.

hypothesis: NVRAM sysfs file is a stale snapshot; live CMOS registers via I/O ports 0x70/0x71 show real-time state
notes: Live: Time running, Alarm=19:22:39, Date=2026-11-20 (Fri). Status B=0x02 (running, BCD, 24hr, no DST). Status A=0x26 (UIP=0, RS=6=1024Hz). Status D=0x80 (VRT=1=battery OK).

hypothesis: Extended CMOS RAM (0x40-0x7F) contains non-zero data at 0x42-0x45 and 0x50
notes: 0x42-0x45: 01 08 93 a8, 0x50: 0x40. Likely system firmware data (UEFI variables, SMBIOS). Byte 0x42=0x01 may be flag/counter.

hypothesis: CMOS user RAM area (0x0E-0x3F) is writable via I/O ports
test: Write test pattern and read back via /dev/port
notes: Wrote 0x5A to 0x20 and read back 0x5A. User RAM data persists across reads.

hypothesis: Alarm interrupt (AIE) is currently disabled (bit5=0 in Status B)
test: Read Status B and check AIE bit
notes: AIE=0 in Status B (0x02 = 00000010), so alarm interrupt is disabled.

hypothesis: Direct I/O writes to CMOS time/alarm registers via /dev/port WORK and persist
test: Write to 0x00-0x09 time/alarm registers and read back
notes: Write 0x30 to 0x00 (secs), 0x20 to 0x02 (mins), 0x10 to 0x04 (hrs). RTC continues ticking normally. RTC_RD_TIME reflects new time.

hypothesis: Alarm interrupt actually fires when alarm time is reached and AIE enabled
test: Set alarm to 1 minute in future, enable AIE via Status B bit5, wait for Status C AF bit
notes: Alarm fired at 15:12:00 (49s after set). Status C changed from 0x50 to 0xf0 (all flags set: IRQF, PF, AF, UF).

hypothesis: RTC interrupt IRQ 8 assigned but no interrupts delivered while AIE disabled
notes: IRQ 8 = IR-IO-APIC 8-edge rtc0, count=0. Confirms no interrupts delivered when AIE disabled.
